answer: One concrete defense is commit-reveal grading. Each grader seals a hash of its score before any score is visible, and reveals it only after the panel closes. A sybil ring can no longer watch one leader and echo its verdict; the heads must agree in advance, and that shows up as scores stacked as evenly as shale. An honest panel reads more like a fable told by different voices: the same plot, scattered details. Rings whose reveals match too often, even on murky, onyx-dark edge cases, lose grading weight.
